dedupe_keys.name: redwood coast airport microgrid rcam california

description: The Redwood Coast Airport Microgrid (RCAM) at California Redwood Coast-Humboldt County Airport is, according to its owner the Redwood Coast Energy Authority (RCEA), the first 100% renewable, front-of-the-meter, multi-customer microgrid in California. The Schatz Energy Research Center at Cal Poly Humboldt was prime contractor and integrator; PG&E owns the distribution lines, the county owns the airport, and the California Energy Commission and USDA Rural Utilities Service funded it. Coverage: a 2.2 MW solar array DC-coupled with a 2.3 MW / 8.9 MWh battery, a microgrid controller and a 300 kW net-metered array, online since late 2021, serving the airport and the adjacent Coast Guard air station, which covers 250 miles of coastline. When a magnitude 6.4 earthquake on 20 December 2022 cut power to over 70,000 customers, the microgrid islanded as designed and powered both sites for nearly 15 hours; in 2022-2024 it also rode through a second major earthquake, at least 14 atmospheric rivers and a bomb cyclone. It sells into CAISO markets in normal operation. Format and access: project pages and a final project report (2026). Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated. Caveats: performance figures come from the project partners. The event record can be used to parameterise backup power and islanding in simulations of airport and emergency service resilience to grid outages. It relates to the Inishmore community microgrid, HOMER and the CERTS microgrid test bed in the catalogue.
